evidence: 0093 (owner decisions of 2026-10-28, patient parity with hid-1.0; migrations pre-approved for this batch) is additive. Identity's runtime reads identity.patients only through RLS, which lets system:auth see public-enrollment patients alone (0051), so every lookup that must also find a patient migrated from hid-1.0 is a SECURITY DEFINER function with search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp. New functions: auth.find_patient_account(kind, value) (system:auth; by Health ID, phone contact-lookup HMAC (or a Nigerian number's two, its +234 and +2340 forms comma separated, because hid-1.0 stored a trunk 0 typed after +234 and the importer kept it; one account across both or nothing), compared as char(64) so that patients_phone_hmac_uq answers it, or account id; the one active patient's account, any status but deleted, with the workforce flag, the verified-email flag and the patient's first name and Health ID; nothing when none or several accounts match; the password hash only for Health ID and phone) for patient sign-in, recovery start and the reset emails; auth.patient_email_registered(email, HMAC) (system:auth; Google sign-up answers GOOGLE_ACCOUNT_EXISTS); auth.link_google_identity_by_verified_email(subject, email, HMAC) (system:auth; a linked subject answers suspended for a suspended patient, else already_linked; otherwise under an advisory lock on the email, the candidates from two index lookups (accounts_email_ci_uq, patients_email_hmac_uq) unioned: none, ambiguous, workforce, not_verified, suspended, linked_elsewhere, or the link with source_system hid-google-verified-email-link, an auth.google.auto-link audit row and the SECURITY_GOOGLE_LINKED inbox notice; account then patient locked FOR UPDATE as 0059; unique (issuer, subject) settles a race as already_linked); auth.record_account_security_notice(account, code) (system:auth; SECURITY_PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTED, SECURITY_PASSWORD_CHANGED, SECURITY_GOOGLE_LINKED, resource type account, no resource id, empty metadata, for the account's active patient only, only with evidence of the last 10 minutes, once per evidence, a reset request at most hourly; null otherwise, never raising); identity.count_my_unread_notifications(subject, session) (live patient session; unread inbox plus unread imported hid-1.0 items, each counted to 1000, at most 1000); identity.patient_self_access_log(subject, session, limit, before) (live patient session; newest first, the patient's own successful application audit events of record views and changes (document downloads and OCR source reads, OCR reads, routed orders sent and withdrawn, read, accepted, marked cannot complete or wrong patient, or corrected by the receiving laboratory or pharmacy, and work items accepted among them), access grants and ends and emergency access, read through audit_patient_time_idx, at most 2000 rows a call, consecutive views or changes by one person at one facility under 10 minutes apart as one entry; each entry id, at, action, actorKind, actorName (clinician), facilityName; never a record, resource id, reason, address or user agent; keyset next). Replaced bodies, each pinned by md5 of pg_proc.prosrc before (0092's bd9190beca14e04b46eb3399910dcd73, 0010's 16b9fd3d2fe5d6f803d532e1dd0f91a7) and after (b21ffc9d2426c988b0b358e5718542ed, d13df3197640316324948268d7d9a18f): identity.activate_public_patient_signup, 0092's body byte for byte but the profile phone rule ^\+234[0-9]{10}$ becoming ^\+[1-9][0-9]{6,14}$ (E.164 of any country); identity.close_own_consent_grant, 0010's body plus the CONSENT_GRANT_ENDED_BY_CLINICIAN inbox notice (resource consent-grant, the grant id, metadata facilityName only, never the reason) when an active grant is closed before it expires, never on a replay; their answers, audit rows, refusals, owners, ACLs, language, volatility and search_path unchanged (post-checked in the migration). Preconditions (55000, nothing applied): prerequisites exist; no object of 0093 exists under any signature (already applied); the two replaced bodies and 17 relied-on bodies pinned by md5; the inbox code, resource type and metadata CHECKs, audit_patient_time_idx and the patients' Health ID and phone unique indexes pinned by definition; the applying role holds, by ownership, membership or grant and never a superuser's bypass, ownership of identity.patients and every privilege the new bodies need, owns the replaced functions, and the close's owner may run the inbox writer and read identity.facilities (42501 otherwise). Locks: none on any application table and none on any existing function (no table, index, CHECK or trigger is created or altered; every body is PL/pgSQL; section 0 reads catalogs only). Measured with pg_locks before commit: ACCESS SHARE on the auth and identity schemas, the plpgsql language and the two runtime roles; SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on five new functions (comments); ACCESS EXCLUSIVE only on the migration's own temporary table and helper and the session's temporary schema. Grants: the six new functions to hid_identity_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime (revoked from PUBLIC), in the migration and in runtime-grants.sql; the replaced functions keep their ACLs. Measured on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster with the repository's runner: 0001-0092 applied and roles bootstrapped, then 0093 planned, dry-run and applied (33 ms), a rerun found 0 pending, the file applied again stopped with 55000 0093: already applied, the role bootstrap and verify-roles passed; a fresh database took 0001-0093 in one dry run and one apply; a copy whose schemas, tables and functions belong to a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner applied 0093 as that owner; a copy with a drifted replaced body (close) or relied-on body (the inbox writer) stopped with nothing applied, and so did an applying role that does not own identity.patients or the replaced function. All 16 database/tests and 49 test/database suites pass on the upgraded and the fresh copy, among them the new patient-parity-identity suite (security properties and grants; international, 7-digit and Nigerian sign-up phones activate, a number without + is refused, a replay unchanged; a migrated patient found by Health ID and phone where RLS hides it, by either of a Nigerian number's two HMACs, two accounts across them answering nothing, the phone through patients_phone_hmac_uq and the Google candidates through accounts_email_ci_uq and patients_email_hmac_uq with 2,000 analyzed other patients, suspended, workforce, deleted and malformed cases, system:auth only; every Google outcome with the link, audit and notice rows; security notices with evidence, dedupe and refusals, the explicit link's and a completed recovery's notices; the early-end notice once, none on replay, after expiry or for a deleted login, the close's answer and audit unchanged, another clinician P0002; the unread count bound to the live session; the access log's kinds, exclusions, names, collapsing, keyset pages, scan cap and session binding, document downloads, OCR reads and routed orders as views and changes; each fix reverted alone fails it), and seven definer suites pass with the NOSUPERUSER owner. A patient with 300,000 audit rows among 1,300,000 reads a 50- or 100-entry page in 70-110 ms, a page 200 days back in 35-60 ms (2,000-row index scan about 1 ms). On a copy with 50,000 patients a phone lookup takes 0.3 ms (an index scan of patients_phone_hmac_uq; a text comparison read every patient, 21 ms) and an unlinked Google sign-in's candidates 0.09 ms (index scans of accounts_email_ci_uq and patients_email_hmac_uq; one OR across both tables joined every patient, 36 ms). Old images on this schema: the previous Identity calls none of the new functions; its direct Health ID query still finds public-enrollment patients only, as before; its sign-up sends +234 numbers, which the replaced activation admits; a clinician's close answers as before with one more inbox row, which the previous website shows with its generic title. Applied migrations 0001-0092 are unchanged.
